title: Beyond Nutritional Adequacy: A Safety Window–Guided Framework for Therapeutic Nutrient Exploration in Integrative Orthomolecular Systems Medicine
content: Dietary reference intakes define nutritional requirements and population risk, but do not establish every disease-specific therapeutic exposure. Richard Z. Cheng's Integrative Orthomolecular Systems Medicine (I-OM) hypothesis is that selected nutrient–indication–population combinations may benefit from exposure beyond conventional adequacy at acceptable incremental risk. This article develops a Safety Window–Guided Therapeutic Exploration Principle for testing that hypothesis. A purposive narrative evidence map integrates nutrient risk assessment, controlled studies, uncontrolled clinical series and traceable orthomolecular observations. An operational record separates physiological status, clinical benefit, observed tolerability, adverse outcomes and uncertainty, and links these to staged research decisions. Vitamin D illustrates the method: prediabetes and demyelinating-disease studies provide indication-specific signals, while historical and modern high-exposure reports extend the observed exposure range. These findings coexist with null prevention trials, hypercalciuria, skeletal effects, regimen-dependent falls and fractures, and documented intoxication. Assigned dose, achieved serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and treatment duration answer different questions. The 50–100 and 100–150 ng/mL intervals are candidate research strata, not established effective or safe bands; approximately 150 ng/mL is not a universal toxicity threshold. Existing-exposure analyses can evaluate the latter interval and define what further evidence would justify a prospective study. Vitamin C, thiamine, magnesium, vitamin B6, niacin, iodine and selenium illustrate nutrient-specific opportunities and constraints. TPIM integrates safety, effectiveness/scientific plausibility, affordability and accessibility. The proposed contribution is a testable decision process for therapeutic exploration, not a new intake ceiling. Its value and the underlying therapeutic hypotheses require empirical evaluation.
